conflicts: 6s5d 3D hyperfine constants: the Gustavsson 1979 abstract (used here) gives 137Ba A(3D1)=-520.536(3), B=17.890(3); A(3D2)=415.928(3), B=25.899(13); A(3D3)=456.559(4), B=47.390(16). arXiv:2512.07603 (Tang) Tables V/VII quote, citing the same paper, -520.602(6)/17.950(8), 415.841(30)/25.756(50), 456.548(6)/47.302(60) (and for 135Ba B = 11.690(8), 16.522(54), 30.800(62)); probably uncorrected vs second-order-corrected constants, not verified because the full paper is paywalled.

6s5d 1D2 hyperfine: Schmelling abstract -82.180(3)/59.564(14) MHz (137Ba), B(135)=38.710(15); Tang quotes -82.180(6), 59.568(19), 38.713(20) for the same reference. Schmelling's own 3D2/3D3 values (A=413.9(9), 455.4(16) MHz) are superseded by Gustavsson.

6s6p 1P1 lifetime: 8.37(8) ns (quoted by Dzuba & Ginges), 8.2(2) ns (Lurio 1964), 8.0(5) ns (Dammalapati thesis), 8.4 ns (Leschhorn, from 18.9 MHz linewidth); NIST A = 1.19e8 s^-1 corresponds to 8.40 ns.
5d6p 3D3 lifetime: 10.2(1.5) ns measured (Brink 1980, Hanle) vs 18 ns theory and 15 ns from NIST A values.
5d6p 3D1 -> 6s2 1S0 (413 nm): A = 1.3(1)e6 (De et al. 2009, own measurement) vs 1.5(2)e6 (Niggli & Huber 1987) vs NIST 1.46e6; branching 2.3(2)(1)% (De thesis) / 2.2(2)% (PRA text) vs 2.6(3)%.
6s6p 1P1 -> 6s5d 3D1 branching: PRA 79, 041402 text prints B_ir3 = 4.2(4)e-5, but its own Table I rates give 3.1e3/1.19e8 = 2.6e-5. Not entered as a branching value.

6s6p 3P1 infrared branches: Dammalapati thesis Table 4.3 prints 3D2 at 2723.0 nm with 1.2e5 and 3D1 at 2923.3 nm with 3.2e5 (labels swapped / typo); the EPJD paper and De thesis give 3D2: 2923.0 nm, 3.18(32)e5 and 3D1: 2775.7 nm, 1.23(12)e5, which agrees with the NIST level energies and is used here.

1107.8 nm (3D1-1P1) odd-isotope shifts of Dammalapati et al. (-114(4), -39(4) MHz) break King-plot linearity and disagree with theory (Naze et al.: 67.2, 132.1 MHz) and with the shifts implied by the direct 413 nm measurement (arXiv:2311.08954); treat the odd-isotope 1107.8 and 1130.6 nm values with caution.
413 nm isotope shift of 134Ba: 124.3(1.3) in the abstract and Table II of arXiv:2311.08954, 125.3(1.3) in its Table I.
6s6p 3P0 lifetime (theory): 2.6 us (Dzuba & Flambaum 2007) vs 2.86 us (Dzuba & Ginges 2006); 6s6p 3P1 theory 1.2 us vs measured 1.345(14) us.
not_found: Absolute frequency of 553.7 nm 6s2 1S0 - 6s6p 1P1: no comb-referenced measurement located (searched arXiv / web); use the NIST level 18060.261 cm^-1.

Measured lifetimes of 6s5d 3D1, 3D2, 3D3, 1D2 (metastable): none located; arXiv:2607.11282 states explicitly that 1D2 has no measured lifetime. Theory values entered for 3D2 and 1D2 only; no number found for 3D1 or 3D3 (Shi: 3D3 'over 100 s', details only in its supplement).
Measured lifetimes of 6s6p 3P0, 3P2: none located; theory entered.

Measured lifetimes of 6s7p 1P1 and 3P1 and g_J of 6s7p/5d6p levels: Brecht, Kowalski, Lido, Ma, zu Putlitz, Z. Phys. 264, 273 (1973) exists but is paywalled (Springer); a search-engine snippet gave 13.5(6) ns (6s7p 1P1) and 85.0(8.0) ns (6s7p 3P1), NOT verified on the page and therefore not entered. Theory values entered instead.

Measured lifetimes of 6s7s 3S1, 6s7s 1S0, 6s6d, 5d2, 5d6p 3P/1P/1D/1F/3F4 levels: no accessible source. Candidates behind paywalls: Zhang et al., Phys. Rev. A 82, 042507 (2010) (70 odd levels from 30815.512 cm^-1 upward, 11.3-901 ns); JQSRT 2019 'Radiative lifetime measurements ... high-lying levels in Ba I'; Matsuo et al., Phys. Rev. A 59, 2071 (1999) (5d6p levels); Kelly & Mathur, Can. J. Phys. 55, 83 (1977) (1P1). Theory (Dzuba & Flambaum 2007) entered for all of these.

Hyperfine constants of 6s6p 3P2 (Keim et al., Z. Phys. D 18, 117 (1991), 137Ba, paywalled), of 5d6p levels other than 3D1 (Grundevik et al., Z. Phys. A 306, 195 (1982) and 312, 1 (1983), paywalled), and of 6s7s, 6s6d, 6s7p, 5d2 levels: not accessible.
Isotope shifts of 1500.4 nm (1D2-1P1), 667.7 nm and the other 6s5d-5d6p lines near 700 nm (Grundevik 1982/1983, paywalled): not accessible; 135-138 shift of 1130.6 nm not measured.

A_s values for lines NIST already lists (553.7, 1107.9, 1130.6, 791.4, 413.4, 659.7, 667.7 nm) are repeated only because the source gives an uncertainty or a newer measurement.
